## Specific RQ: 
What are some ways child development is negatively impacted by their use of social media.

## Data set names:
Social Media and the Internet in the Trafficking of Humans (SMITH)
Counter Trafficking Data Collaborative (CTDC) Synthetic Data 

## Trustworthiness/reputability
We found that both data sets include a codebook explaining their variables. The CTDC codebook details every variable. It provides variable definition, its data type and it lists the possible outputs of all variables. Whereas the SMITH data set only describes variables that are abstract. For example the variable “country” is straight forward and it is not detailed in the codebook. This may lead to issues as the reader may misinterpret a variable's definition or the variable type. 

We must acknowledge that the CTDC data set is synthetic. It was created from software developed by Microsoft. It compares existing data models to standardize large amounts of data on human trafficking cases across multiple platforms. To maintain the victims anonymity, variable outputs are given as intervals. This creates an impact on the accuracy of data labels and their outputs. For example, instead of listing the direct relationship between the victim and perpetrator, we are told if both knew each other or if they were strangers. This data collection method may interfere with our final conclusions as the sense of vagueness from the data set will carry on to our final conclusions. 

## Relevance to RQ:
The SMITH data set is a collection of information on human trafficking cases reported to the United Nations. This means our final generalizations will apply to UN member countries. Also it’s important to note cases of human trafficking may go unreported

Even though the variable names and their outputs from the CTDC data set are vague, we are still able to draw credible conclusions from analysis. 

The SMITH data set has about 1,500 observations and the CTDC data set has about 21,000 observations. So If we could add anything to our data, we would add more data to our data. A larger sample size for the SMITH data would allow for greater confidence in our final results

Most of the variables from the CTDC data set are proxies. As their goal was to retain victim privacy.

## Ethical soundness
Discretions and victim protection is a huge roadblock for our topic of research. We have found difficulties in even finding a proficient dataset related to our topic.

## Scope 
Minors and adults are reported as victims in both data sets. Again the SMITH data set has information on human trafficking within member countries of the United Nations and The CTDC data set specifies what continent the victim comes from.

Originally we wanted to explore relationships between child development and their use of social media. We faced ethical constraints trying to look for this information. So we decided to explore different topics and now the development aspect of our original research question is missing from both data sets. However both data sets include children and the SMITH data set relates their human trafficking cases to social media. 

In conclusion with our combined data sets we can make claims about human trafficking for all ages and from most countries. Again, we can not touch on the intended topic of child development.
